Sibuna v0.3.0 adds a native OWASP Core Rule Set engine (SID 0010). Signed CRS 4.30.0 releases
are verified against the pinned CRS key, compiled in-process and inspected in Off, Audit or
Enforce mode on both reverse-proxy and forward-auth (headers profile) deployments. Selection,
rollback, private sample tests, rule-change reviews, exclusions and per-finding evidence are
managed through the console or the native `sibuna crs` commands, with three-node convergence.

The engine evaluates CRS with linear-time matching: a bounded lazy DFA decides regexes, the
ordered Pike simulation defines capture groups only when a rule uses them, and identical
transform pipelines share one result per value within a phase. JSON and XML bodies are parsed
by Content-Type, as in ModSecurity's recommended configuration.

Qualification:
- The pinned CRS FTW corpus runs through the actual daemon: 5,107 complete contracts pass
  in Audit, and 5,123 of 5,193 tests satisfy their rule-ID/status assertions. Fifteen regex-log
  gaps and one incomplete work-bound case remain explicit. Other differences reproduce
  ModSecurity 3.0.14 or are strict acquisition and deliberate connector refusals. The pinned
  overlong-argument work-bound case returns 403 with zero origin bytes in Enforce; Audit
  permits it under its configured policy and records incomplete coverage.
- Three-node selection, failover, quorum refusal, restart and rollback pass on separate hosts.
- With the load generator on a separate host and four product CPUs, paranoia level one serves
  10,787 small GETs per second (47,311 with CRS disabled), 1,151 8 KiB JSON POSTs and 4,248
  16 KiB multipart uploads, at 133.8-140.5 MiB peak RSS. No sample reached the work limit.
  The five-round, 16-connection run includes eight dashboards and identifies clean revision
  d461e7f, after the final application corrections. CPU frequency and unrelated physical-host
  activity remain uncontrolled; the results are not a matched BunkerWeb comparison.

Behaviour changes:
- Request targets must be origin-form (or `OPTIONS *`); absolute-form, `CONNECT` and fragments
  receive 400. Repeated, missing (HTTP/1.1) or malformed `Host` fields receive 400.
- CRS transaction slots are tiered: spare reservation becomes small slots for requests up to
  64 KiB, and a busy pool waits up to 50 ms before answering 503.
- The default CRS work budget is 128 million units. Selections saved by earlier builds keep
  their stored budget. Change Work budget in a console candidate or supply complete reviewed
  settings with `crs update --settings`, then select it. Local-directory updates accept
  `--crs-work-budget`; startup flags must agree with an existing saved selection.
- Malformed JSON or XML declared by Content-Type is an inspection failure (403 in Enforce).
- Cluster catch-up preserves ballot-bearing leader evidence while replaying chosen history.
  Startup retries temporary storage unavailability before opening listeners.

Downloads:
- Linux x86-64 and ARM64: statically linked musl builds; Linux 5.10 or later.
- macOS Apple Silicon and Intel: macOS 15 or later; unsigned command-line builds.
- Windows x86-64: native sibuna.exe; Windows 10 / Server 2019 or later.

Archives include the executable, README, full license texts, dependency notices and an exact
build manifest. SHA256SUMS covers every archive. Engine sources are LGPL-3.0; console
sources, including the Wasm interface, are AGPL-3.0. The combined executable is AGPL-covered.
CRS rules are Apache-2.0 and are downloaded and verified at runtime, not bundled.
Corresponding source and build scripts are in this release's tag and linked from the console.
Companies seeking alternative licensing can contact the authors, Vikrant Rathore and
Ronak Rathore. Third-party libraries remain subject to their respective licenses.

The shipped builds include storage and console support; the console starts only with --console.
Multi-node deployments require a separate -Dcluster=true build with OpenSSL 3. No GeoIP address
database is bundled; use the documented CLI import/update commands for your chosen dataset.

Terminate public HTTPS at a trusted ingress and forward private HTTP/1.1 to Sibuna. With CRS
disabled, uploads stream to the origin and the lightweight inspector covers the first 8 KiB.
Admitted WebSockets relay bytes without message inspection. Forward-auth sees only metadata
supplied by the ingress. Local rate limits are not global quotas, and Sibuna does not provide
volumetric network mitigation.

The strict SID 0007 console-impact target is still not formally passed. Published benchmarks retain their
measured revision and host description and are not guarantees for other hosts.

Documentation: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/
Deployment guide: https://insanai.github.io/sibuna/book/operations.html
Source: https://github.com/insanai/sibuna/tree/v0.3.0
